newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr closes well bid as dollar-yen weakens.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr closes well bid as dollar-yen weakens.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed well bid on Thursday as the greenback continued its plunge against the yen.
Dealers said that with the Trade-Weighted Index down at 67.77 there were plenty of kiwi buyers around.
At 5.30 p.m. the kiwi was at US$0.6964/71, slightly up on its 0.6961/68 opening and against the 0.6930/37 Wednesday close.
Dealers said there was still good demand for the kiwi arising from eurokiwi issues.

A 100 basis-point fall in dollar-yen roughly translates into a 15 basis point move in the TWI. Dealers said that given the dollar's fall from over 126 yen early last week to under 116 today the TWI should theoretically have been 1.5 points lower.
Instead, the market had countered that by taking the kiwi higher. However, failure on several occasions to penetrate 0.6965-70 suggested it could be hitting a ceiling, dealers said.

Comments from Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara that the the Group of Seven agreement on foreign exchange markets had filtered through sufficiently were expected to stem the dollar's slide.
